newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Human rights body asks OSCE to suspend Belarus.
newsitem.headline: Human rights body asks OSCE to suspend Belarus.

text.p: An international human rights group urged Europe's top security body on Monday to suspend Belarus from membership following a controversial referendum last month that significantly increased the powers of its president.

"We take this step...based upon our analysis of recent political and human rights developments in the country," the Vienna-based Helsinki Federation for Human Rights said in a letter addressed to the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) chairman, Flavio Cotti.

"Belarus should...be suspended from membership in the OSCE pending its tangible re-commitment to democratic principles, human rights and the rule of law," said the letter, a copy of which was made available to Reuters.
Belarussian President Alexander Lukashenko has come under strong criticism from the West which has accused him of building dictatorial powers.

Cotti, chairing the OSCE's two-day summit now under way in Lisbon, rapped Lukashenko in his opening speech on Monday, telling him the growing crisis in his country should be resolved through dialogue and that he was "deeply concerned" by developments in Belarus.
